Declaration is NOT a filter for run inputs (history replay passes through unchanged). S1-S4 done.

Element self-healing: consume captured candidate selectors at runtime, pre-action validation (visibility/disabled/occlusion), classified element errors, and fix the declared-but-unimplemented input params (keyIntervalMs, clipboard)

Browser command param contract: implement declared-but-inert click params (simulateHuman/clickPosition with point-accurate occlusion precheck), forward cookie filters and tabId, drop unreachable screenshot/close params, and gate every declared param against actual executor consumption

Desktop command param contract: the param-consumption gate covers all four channels (78 commands, 0 skipped); every declared-but-inert desktop param is resolved — wait-for-element timeoutMs, click simulateHuman/clickPosition, attachWindow className on uia — and the two win32 params with no counterpart are dropped. Includes a new error-contract gate (manifest errors must cover returned codes). S1-S5 done.
Browser teardown: close tabs (explicit/all) and terminate ALL processes of the named browser (kill-all semantics; M35 removed the launchedByUs/byProcessName scope)

Element post-capture UX (M39): align the GUI verify button's wording with the Web 'structural check' semantics; surface captured-but-never-shown data (selector.candidates with measured matchedCount, semantic features, page fingerprint, desktop className/name); and an offline element editor (promote a candidate to primary with swap semantics, checkbox the desktop locator fields scoped per backend, in-place structural validation). S1-S3 done.

GUI responsiveness (M40): stop scanning run artifacts on the startup critical path (reuse one list_runs for both flow library and run history; defer_refresh so the window paints before data loads), detect a connected-but-unresponsive extension leg via the capture_armed ack (3s grace, 30s degraded budget, real reason surfaced instead of a silent 90s wait), and give capture a visible face plus an exit (always-on-top capture float with per-leg status and a cancel button; second click on Capture cancels the running session; work() always emits so an exception can no longer wedge the session; late results from a replaced session are dropped). Second round (same-day follow-up report: the first click of a workbench tab / the first open of the element library is the slow one, and restarting the app seems to fix it): measurement showed round one had only MOVED the scan block from before the window appears to right after it, i.e. onto the user's first click (three-arm A/B: first tab click delayed 202.3ms -> 8.9ms). So the artifact scan is now sliced: run_history exposes iter_run_summaries()+sort_runs() with list_runs built from both, and HomeWindow.start_refresh() fills the flow library immediately then drains the run scan in 6ms slices across event-loop turns (pending rows show an ellipsis, never 'not run'); a sync refresh supersedes an in-flight slice so a stale scan cannot overwrite fresh data. The editor pre-warms the element-library dock on first show (first open 65.2ms -> paid in idle).

M41: the capture highlight frame clears the mouse cursor — desktop `_HoverOverlay` now grows the element rect by OUTSET=5 (frame band lands element-external [2,5) = BORDER 3 + 2px cursor hotspot) instead of insetting it, and the in-page picker box does the same while dropping its 12% red fill (real-hardware pixels: 6/13 sample points had cursor pixels covered before, 0/13 after; a separate A/B showed UIA hit-testing was never affected, 0/13 difference — the defect was purely visual). Plus a startup splash: `gui/splash.py` covers the ~976ms pre-window initialization (load_catalog 420ms first-run incl. lazy imports + Qt init 276ms + window ctor 68ms + first frame 211ms, first-sample not median) with a card that does not take keyboard focus, wired through a `with startup_splash(app)` context manager around load_catalog -> window ctor -> show. And S3 (maintainer's second-round clarification: the desktop *capture float window* — a real top-level window with no WS_EX_TRANSPARENT, so it blocks both sight and clicks — must dodge the cursor): `gui/capture_float.py` gains a pure function `capture_float_origin(area, size, cursor)` that parks the window at the bottom-right by default and flips it to the top-left once the cursor enters the default rect grown by AVOID_PAD=80. The judging baseline is always the *default* rect, never the window's current position, so the behaviour is stateless and does not oscillate; `avoid_cursor(cursor)` replaces `place_bottom_right()`, honours a new `user_positioned` flag (once the user drags it, automation stops moving it), and `gui/app.py` drives it on a 40ms tick (~25Hz, far faster than the 500ms status refresh, otherwise a fast flick overtakes the window). And S4 (maintainer, same day: 「有个 90 秒的倒计时，是必须的吗？用户角度来说没必要」) drops the countdown *display* from that float window while keeping the 90s timeout itself: the cap is the only backstop when both capture legs wedge (bridge endpoint alive but extension not listening -> page leg never arms -> desktop leg yields in hybrid -> user waits silently — the exact M40 bug report), so CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS stays as the session layer deadline; but rendering it as a ticking 剩余 N 秒 is information-free (a normal capture ends in seconds, and a timeout carries no penalty) and misrepresents a backstop as a deadline. capture_float.py loses time_label / tick() and show_capture() no longer takes timeout_seconds; app.py's _tick_capture_float keeps only the leg-status refresh (the 500ms timer still turns the web row red once the extension leg is declared dead), _capture_budget and _capture_started_at are deleted as now-reader-less fields, and the status-bar timeout text drops its visible 90 秒. Guarded by test_capture_float_never_shows_a_countdown, which asserts on the float window's real label texts (no 剩余, no N 秒) plus the absence of the tick method and of the timeout_seconds parameter — negative-verified with 3 independent injections, each landing on its own assertion line. Fourth-round follow-up (S5): the 90s backstop ITSELF is removed, not just its display. Re-checking every exit path showed it guards only "the user walked away" — a capture result, both legs going dead (_exhausted settles immediately rather than waiting for the deadline) and user cancel (float button / second click on 捕获元素 / Esc, where ExtensionCaptureSession.cancel() unconditionally sets the result event and settles in under 1s) all settle without it, and since capture runs on a daemon thread the cancel button stays clickable throughout; meanwhile it cost the user real work, silently dropping an already-picked element whenever a careful pick ran past 90s. It was never a contract either: CLI --timeout and devserver timeoutSeconds are caller-supplied defaults, only the GUI hard-coded it. CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS becomes float("inf") so the wait is the user's call (inf works end to end: now + inf = inf, now < inf holds, and the parent-side slice min(0.5, inf - now) is still 0.5). Guarded by test_capture_never_gives_up_on_its_own (three assertions: the constant is inf, inf survives the constructor call, pick receives that same value), negative-verified with 3 independent injections hitting :654/:661/:664 respectively. Same round: S1's outline outset was kept per the maintainer's call, and the "full suite slowed from 177s to 300s+" question was investigated and closed as a host-level transient (three mechanisms disproved with controls: the sandbox delete guard via a same-window A/B on CODEBUDDY_TOOL_CALL_ID, process startup/import/collection, and Qt init; plus a 25-round sentinel probe that never caught the window). Full gate now PASSES: 1206 passed / 21 skipped / 2 xfailed in 183.74s, exit 0, 202s total (the two previously-red QProcess cases passed too). See M41 task sheet 5.4.

M42: web capture on pages that were already open, and no leftover red frame. Declarative content_scripts inject only at page load, so after the extension is (re)loaded an already-open tab either has no capture script or keeps a zombie whose extension context is gone (chrome.runtime.id undefined, sendMessage throws 'Extension context invalidated'). broadcast() sent and silently swallowed the failure, so capture_arm never reached those pages ('does not take effect on the page I already had open'); the zombie kept drawing the highlight from its own armed flag, never received capture_disarm, and the failed-capture path deliberately kept the box ('the red frame is still there after capture'). Fixed on both sides because neither half works alone: background.js back-injects content.js into tabs whose sendMessage failed (http(s)/file only, arm only, never on disarm) and re-sends the arm, arms only after persisting the flag (a back-injected script reads storage.session on startup), and disarms on host disconnect (the push model has no heartbeat, so a lost disarm leaves the page permanently armed). content.js replaces the install-once guard with an instance registry {alive, teardown}: a live instance still short-circuits duplicate injection while a zombie is torn down first (overlays cleared, every listener unbound through a recyclable helper) and then superseded; onMove self-heals once the context is gone and a failed capture now drops the frame but keeps the hint. Extension version 0.4.0 -> 0.4.1.

M43: pressing Esc during capture must end the capture session, not just hide the red frame. `cancelled` is a session-level signal but was handled as a single-leg failure: the desktop hover leg reports {"cancelled": true} when Esc is pressed (the only desktop producer; the agent then exits and its `finally: overlay.destroy()` makes the red frame disappear), and because that payload carries no `kind` HybridCaptureSession.pick recorded it as `desktop_failure` - the same bucket as an agent crash. `_exhausted()` only closes the session once BOTH legs are out, and the extension leg (endpoint connected) stays alive, so with the host passing timeout_seconds=inf (M41 S5 CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) the session never ends: window still minimized, extension still armed, `_capture_session` still set, and starting capture again still says one is already running - exactly the report 'pressing Esc on the desktop only hides the red frame, it is still in capture mode'. The symmetric case (Esc in the page: content.js onKey -> rpa-capture-cancelled -> sendCapture({cancelled:true})) hit the same shape while the desktop agent kept polling global keys. The old code did have a cancelled branch, but only in `_exhausted_result` - reachable only after both legs are out, which never happens for a cancel, so it was an unreachable cancellation path (now removed). Fix: `_is_cancelled()` distinguishes cancel from failure; both leg branches in `pick` now call `_finish_cancelled()` which disarms the extension and reclaims the desktop agent. Tests pin three layers (session-level result, closing timing, both legs reclaimed) and a paired case keeps a leg *failure* from being treated as a cancel.

M44: capture dialog is now the element editor itself (Yingdao parity, P1 slice). The confirm dialog used to expose one editable text line (css for browser, raw locator JSON for desktop) plus read-only candidate text, so editing an element meant: capture -> save -> open the element library -> Edit. Yingdao edits in the same window the capture lands in, and half of the gap was workflow position, not widgets. Fix in five parts. (1) content.js now returns the ancestor chain (selector.path, one {tag,id,classes,nthOfType,fragment} entry per level, max depth 6) by refactoring cssSelectorFor into pathFor(el).map(e=>e.fragment).join(" > ") - byte-identical output, one source for both the executed selector and the node tree; plus the blue capture cursor (Ctrl/Cmd pressed during capture injects a #2F6BFF SVG cursor with !important, cleared on keyup/Esc/disarm/teardown/supersede, clearCaptureCursor removes via its own reference first and falls back to getElementById). (2) The editor form (browser css + candidate promote / desktop locator checkboxes / in-place model validation) is extracted into ElementEditorForm so the capture dialog and the library editor share one implementation instead of two drifting ones (27 existing judgments unchanged through a __getattr__ shell). (3) ElementDialog embeds that form: browser edits the primary css and promotes candidates in place, desktop ticks locator fields - no JSON editing anywhere; the dialog only validates the element name, selector legality stays with the model judgments. (4) Three exits like Yingdao: Save / Save and continue / Recapture via intent(); save-and-continue and recapture restart the capture session right after the dialog closes (session identity guard and late-result drop unchanged); _confirm_element_save returns (intent, payload) while keeping its name so the four existing modal-dialog stubs keep intercepting (a rename would silently unstub and hang offscreen). (5) Offline node tree: path levels render as checkable rows; unchecking ancestors rewrites the primary css as the join of the remaining fragments (one-way: the css field stays the single write-back target), tree state is derived from the current css when rebuilt (shortest suffix match) so a previously shortened selector is not clobbered, and the leaf level cannot be unchecked. selector.path is optional and validated when present (non-empty tag/fragment per level) inside the selector dict - top-level unknown keys are dropped by pydantic. Negative verification 10/10 (probe .harness/spike/probe_m44_negative.py): control-run green, byte-exact injection, N failed without N error / named node-gate check hit, byte-identical restore by md5.

M45: editor UI L1 catch-up (Yingdao parity). The capture-confirm editor gains the property table (per-attribute checkbox with equals/contains match modes compiled back into the css fragment - [class*=".."] for contains, #id kept for equals-per-capture-convention), a unified default element name generator shared bit-for-bit across GUI and Web via one case table (el_{kind}, ordinal on collision - replacing the Web timestamp scheme that degenerated to element_* for desktop), library search/filter (display-only, name or locator substring), and two M44 leftovers fixed: restart paths no longer restore-then-reminimize the main window (the visible flash) and candidate promotion now re-syncs the node-tree check states from the new css immediately. No executor contract touched: querySelectorAll still consumes the compiled css; the JS side of the name generator is slice-evaluated against the same case table as Python (either side drifting turns at least one gate red).

M46: element reference model (B1 decision, Yingdao-isomorphic). Flow nodes carry elementRefs (arg key -> element name) alongside the value snapshot in with_; the orchestrator resolves referenced args from the per-flow elements/ store before schema validation, so editing an element's main locator in the library takes effect for already-inserted instructions on the next run with zero flow edits (the Yingdao repair-experience premise). Missing or corrupt element documents fall back to the snapshot and emit an observable elementRefFallback event (never the silent candidate decay of the css-reverse-lookup path). GUI insert dual-writes ref + snapshot; manually editing a referenced arg in the param form takes ownership and drops the ref. Old flow files without elementRefs run unchanged (None = pure value-copy semantics); extra=forbid still rejects unknown keys. Decision recorded in ADR-001 after the maintainer confirmed option 2 based on reverse-engineered Yingdao storage (flow.json stores element codes, xbot_selectors/ stores the values).

M47 S1: live element verification (C2 on an on-demand channel). The capture-confirm dialog gains a Verify button for browser elements that sends capture_verify over a short-lived dedicated bridge connection (independent sessionId/requestId, no capture-session keep-alive: the page is already disarmed after capture and verification only needs a reachable content script plus the scripting API - the on-demand channel avoids the session-ownership, late-result and timeout lifecycle rework entirely). Background forwards to the focused active tab only (the page the element came from), injects content.js first when missing, and replies capture_verify_result paired by requestId; the content script runs querySelectorAll, flashes yellow boxes (z-index below the capture red frame, auto-cleared after 1600ms) and answers with contentBuild for stale-extension reconciliation. ElementVerifier pairs replies by requestId, times out hard (verify-timeout, never hangs - the M40 lesson) and returns structured errors (extension-offline / bad-reply / passthrough) that the dialog shows inline. Every failure mode is observable, none silent.

M47.1: live preview highlight (C3 on the M47 on-demand channel). The capture_verify envelope gains a mode field (flash/preview/clear); content.js turns flashing highlights into persistent boxes for preview (always clearing the previous round first, including when count=0 - a stale box impersonating a hit is the most dangerous silent mislead) and clear removes them. ElementEditorForm (shared by the capture-confirm dialog and the library editor) gains an injectable live-preview callback: css edits debounce 500ms then run the channel on a worker thread, showing the live hit count inline; stale replies are dropped by sequence pairing; empty css clears instead of querying; dialogs emit finished -> clear so no yellow box outlives the editor; entering capture mode also sweeps leftover preview boxes. EXT_BUILD 0.5.0 -> 0.6.0.

M49: GUI experience polish (P0-P3). A single color source (gui/theme.py) replaces inline hex literals across 13 modules, enforced by an AST scan of string constants plus a must-have list so definitions and references cannot be deleted together. The status bar splits into a color dot plus text (green online / grey benign-offline / red real problem) and stops rewriting setText on an unchanged state so the 5s poll no longer jitters the bar width. gui/persist.py (explicit IniFormat/UserScope) remembers window geometry, the three-pane splitter ratios and dialog sizes, falling back to factory values on corrupt input. A View menu manages five lazily-created docks plus a restore-default-layout action, and a dock closed by the user writes its check state back. Informational modals degrade to inline hint.setText (a whitelist gate compares body text, not titles, since valid modals and retired scenarios can share a title). Back-to-home closes once (previously ask-discard then ask-save fired twice); gui/motion.py transitions are disable-able via RPA_GUI_ANIMATIONS=0 and are fail-safe (disabled or broken animations must leave windows fully visible). gui/fonts.py is the single pixel-size source - the pt/px mix traced back to a pixel base making pointSizeF() return -1, turning derived sizes from 'one step smaller' into 'no size', so the fix uses one unit and falls back to BASE_PX. Ctrl+P opens a command palette over one table with two row kinds (commands insert into the canvas, nodes navigate), with rank_entries as a pure function and palette_prompt as a module-level seam. Verified by 23 negative-verification injections, each byte-restored and md5-checked.

M50: GUI rewrite entry for desktop locators (ancestor chain + anchor). M48 rendered locator.path (ancestor chain) and locator.anchor read-only; M50 upgrades both to editable. path: a permanently-present 4-column editable table (controlType/automationId/name/className) with add-level / remove-selected / move-up / move-down buttons; a level with no keys is dropped (hinted in the UI) via the shared pure function model.desktop.prune_locator_steps, which the capture side (_locator_step_for) and the editor (_commit_path_steps) both use, so the editor does not become a second authority. anchor: an 'enable anchor' checkbox plus a single-level inline locator form (backend selector + field rows reusing LOCATOR_FIELDS_BY_BACKEND); unchecking or leaving it empty removes it. Nesting stays impossible because the form exposes no 'add anchor' entry and the model rejects a nested anchor anyway. Round-trip is byte-preserving when untouched. 12 new contract assertions (test_gui_element_editor.py 59 -> 66) and 4 new negative-verification injections (I22-I25). GUI-only per ADR 0016; the Web editor stays frozen.

M47.9: verification target follows the last-activated browser (Yingdao parity). M47.8 stopped both browsers flashing by having each browser self-judge foreground, but that made both silent when the foreground was our own dialog (which steals focus on Verify) - nothing flashed. The host now picks the target instead of guessing it: capture/foreground_window.py walks the Windows Z-order (GetTopWindow + GW_HWNDNEXT, which is exactly the system-maintained activation stack) and returns the first browser window, so non-browser windows (Explorer, our dialog, tooltips) are skipped naturally. Browser detection is by process name only (QueryFullProcessImageNameW against a known table) because Chrome_WidgetWin_1 is shared by Chromium-based custom clients; enumeration caps at 2048 because the real chain runs 400+ deep. ElementVerifier gains target/auto_target and a three-tuple _candidates(), dispatching only to matching endpoints (reusing _endpoint_browser / _target_matches_instance) and falling back to broadcast when the target has no extension installed. bring_front is applied for flash mode only (SetForegroundWindow; preview would steal focus on every keystroke) and failures are harmless. 11 unit + 7 new contract assertions. macOS research only (CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo front-to-back order) - not implemented.

M47.10: capture-confirm dialog UX (three of five maintainer-reported items). (1) The DOM path tree and the attribute table now sit SIDE BY SIDE in a horizontal QSplitter (tree left/narrow, table right/wide) instead of stacked vertically; the attribute-table caption moved above the splitter since it describes the whole region, not the right column. (2) Hit-count copy is de-duplicated: the dialog's own static 'captured hit N' label is no longer added to the layout when a live preview channel is present, because it is a stale value that can contradict the live one once the user edits the css; the single remaining label lives in the editor form (ElementEditorForm.set_hit_label) and the 'Preview:' prefix was dropped (the context already says where it comes from). Desktop elements without a live channel keep the static label. (3) The primary-selector input is now a multiline, height-adaptive SelectorEdit (QPlainTextEdit subclass, 1-4 rows) instead of a QLineEdit, so long ancestor chains wrap instead of having their tail truncated; it keeps the same text()/setText() API so the ~20 call sites did not change and css_edit remains the single persistence point. Lesson learned: SelectorEdit must NOT shadow the native textChanged signal - declaring 'textChanged = Signal(str)' caused super().textChanged to resolve to the subclass signal (never emitted), so setText changed the text but fired nothing (test_editor_browser_blocks_blank_css went red); the native signal stays connectable and the height resync hangs off document().contentsChanged. 4 new contract assertions in test_gui_element_editor.py and 3 in test_gui_panels.py; 5 negative-verification injections (probe_m47_10_negative.py) all hit. Item (2) 'the candidate-locator logic' was investigated with no code change: content.js candidatesFor only offers #id plus 7 attributes, while the primary css is built from class paths, so React/Vue components with neither yield no candidates and runtime self-heal (M28) never fires - the fix is to widen candidate generation, which is scoped together with XPath support in M51. Item (5) XPath is a separate slice (M51). GUI-only.

M51 (pending): widen the locator supply surface - XPath support plus candidate-generation alignment. Two halves that must land together because each touches the same five layers (extension / contract / executor / self-heal / GUI). (A) XPath: content.js and the executor only understand CSS (page_call uses document.querySelectorAll; there is no document.evaluate), so the extension gains XPath querying, selector.kind becomes a contract discriminator (css|xpath), the browser executor and the runtime self-heal (_page_call_with_fallback / _element_candidates) dispatch on it, and the GUI editor offers a kind selector and validates accordingly. (B) Candidate expansion: content.js candidatesFor currently pushes only '#id' and [attr='...'] for data-testid/data-test/data-qa/name/aria-label/placeholder/title, while the primary css comes from pathEntryFor (tag.class + :nth-of-type), so modern components with no id and none of those 7 attributes produce an empty candidate list and runtime self-heal (M28) never actually fires - the maintainer noticed this directly ('I have never seen any candidate locators'). Candidate generation must be aligned with the class path the primary css uses (class combinations, [class*=] forms, attribute combos). Not implemented yet; tracked here so the diagnosis is not lost.
